EITC and ACTC are dropped at random by default (eitc_claim_prob_scale 1.03, actc_claim_prob_scale 1.1 in 2026; credit_claim_urn is a seeded uniform draw per record, records.py:197-199; calcfunctions.py:3237-3244, 4342-4350). Every run sets both scales to 9e99 ("always claim"); probe p02 shows 5 of 10 identical $40,000 single-parent records losing a $1,852.62 EITC under defaults and none with the reform.

Records(..., exact_calculations=True) is used: the default smooths stepped phase-outs. Probe p02: CTC at AGI $401,234 MFJ is $2,100.00 exact (IRC 24(b)(1) $50 per $1,000 or fraction) against $2,138.30 smooth (calcfunctions.py:3348-3352).
Records(data, start_year=2026, gfactors=None, weights=None) does no growth or extrapolation (records.py:35-37, 142); the Calculator stays in 2026 (asserted each run).

soi_iitax is False in 2026 (probe p01): iitax excludes setax, ptax_amc and e09800 and payrolltax includes them plus the employer share (calcfunctions.py IITAX). The four answers are therefore built from components, not from iitax or payrolltax.

The engine computes regular tax from the rate schedules (SchXYZ) for all taxable incomes; the IRS Tax Table (taxable income under $100,000, $50 bands taxed at the band midpoint) can differ by a few dollars. Not adjusted.
The engine computes the EITC by formula (EITCamount, phase-in rate x earnings, phase-out from max(earnings, AGI)); the IRS EIC Table uses $50 bands and can differ by a few dollars. Not adjusted.

Inputs the engine takes as already limited (no cap in its code): e03150 IRA deduction, e03210 student loan interest, e03220 educator expenses, e03290 HSA, e03270 SE health insurance (Adj), e19200 mortgage interest (ItemDed), e07240 tentative saver's credit (limited by tax in NonrefundableCredits), pencon_p/s 401(k) deferrals, e09900 additional tax. Each is computed from statute in map.py.

Sch 1-A inputs (overtime_income, tip_income, auto_loan_interest) are "assumed to already represent the form-qualified amounts" (calcfunctions.py:876-878); the engine applies the caps and phase-outs and the senior deduction from age_head/age_spouse.

Unlisted numeric facts are 0 and unlisted booleans false (board preface). Eligibility conditions for which the board has no fact at all (valid SSNs, the qualifying-child relationship/support/abode tests, W-2 reporting of overtime, tip occupation, auto-loan vehicle qualification, active participation in a rental) are taken as met; facts that the board states for some people (disabled, blind, student status) are false where unlisted.

A household's answer sums every federal return its members file: the main return (head, spouse and all listed dependents) and the own return of any dependent with income (093 Dependent 1, 123 Child 1, 067 Dependent 1). Alternative (main return only) is in variants_2026.csv as main_return_only for the two income-tax lines; payroll tax is per worker and always sums all members.

federal_income_tax_before_refundable_credits = Form 1040 line 22 plus the Schedule 2 income taxes the engine models besides SE tax and Additional Medicare Tax: NIIT (IRC 1411) and the IRC 72(t) additional tax. Alternative: line 22 alone (variant line22_only).

Payroll tax is the federal employee share only: 6.2% OASDI to the 2026 base $184,500, 1.45% HI, and Additional Medicare Tax 0.9% over $200,000/$250,000 (Form 8959, which also counts SE income). Traditional 401(k) deferrals are FICA wages (engine adds pencon back, calcfunctions.py:215-216). Employer disability pay is not treated as FICA wages (variant disability_benefits_fica).

Medical expenses (e17500) = other_medical_expenses + person-paid premiums for every listed person, on the main return. Premiums = health_insurance_premiums_without_medicare_part_b where stated (the aggregate), else other_health_insurance_premiums, never their sum (the glossary describes the second as a component of the first). Over-the-counter health expenses are excluded (IRC 213(b)); variant otc_in_medical. Employer-paid ESI premiums are excluded (IRC 106).

State and local income or sales tax e18400 = the board's state_and_local_tax_2026.csv value, before the cap; real estate taxes e18500 = stated real_estate_taxes; the engine applies the 2026 SALT cap ($40,400, reduced 30% of MAGI over $505,000, floor $10,000).

Employer disability benefits (disability_benefits) are taxable (IRC 105(a); no employee-paid premiums stated): before 65 as Form 1040 line 1h wages, at 65 or over as pension income (e01500/e01700). The 2025 Form 1040 instructions put disability pensions received before the employer's minimum retirement age on line 1h "Other Earned Income" and later ones on lines 5a/5b (sources/i1040gi.txt:1440, 1536-1544, 1821-1826), and the dependent standard deduction worksheet counts line 1z, which includes 1h, as earned income (i1040gi.txt:2313-2315); the plan's minimum retirement age is not stated, so 65 stands in for it. As e00200 the benefit is earned income for the engine's EITC, ACTC and dependent standard deduction. Alternative: unearned pension income at every age (variant disability_benefits_unearned).

survivor_benefits (non-Social-Security survivor benefits) are read as a fully taxable survivor annuity (e01500/e01700). social_security_dependents is Social Security income of the person it is stated on (variant ss_dependents_to_child moves it to the youngest child).

Alimony paid/received (020, 031, 056) is entered in e03500/e00800; the engine's 2026 law (ALD_AlimonyPaid_hc=1, AlimonyReceived_frac_in_AGI=0) treats it as under a post-2018 instrument, so it has no effect. Variant alimony_pre2019.
Unreimbursed employee business expenses go in e20400; miscellaneous itemized deductions are suspended permanently from 2026 (engine ID_Miscellaneous_hc=1), so they have no effect.
